new.n: Burlington train robbers' buried silver, Mississippi bank near Marcus
new.pl: Toward the river from Marcus (5 mi N of Savanna); the caches were "on the Mississippi bank near the robbery", spot not given (about 3 km radius)
new.st: Near midnight on 5 Aug 1902 six masked men flagged Burlington train No. 47 at Marcus, ran the engine and express car up the track and dynamited the Adams Express safe, getting about $2,000-2,500, mostly silver; one robber was killed. They ran the engine north toward Hanover, then crossed by skiff. Detectives later found the skiff sunk with sand in the river near where the gang had "temporarily buried their booty" on the bank, with several half dollars from the pile still in the sand. Four suspects were arrested in January 1903 after a detective traced the skiff to La Crosse. Whether the rest of the silver was ever recovered is not stated. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
new.t: Probably dug up by the gang; D until an outcome is found. River-bank ground may be in the Upper Mississippi River refuge: check the rules for the land there before any detecting.
src: AP, New-York Tribune, 7 Aug 1902; Red Lodge Picket, 8 Aug 1902 (Mount Carroll dispatch) (LoC)
Saginaw News, 10 Jan 1903, p. 1 (La Crosse dispatch; newspapers.com)
acc: River bank, possibly federal refuge land: check the rules first.
pinev: Toward the river from Marcus; cache spot not given
